Research Agenda

Strategic Cognitive Offloading Framework

My research is organized around a single unifying question: how should cognitive effort be optimally distributed between human learners and AI? This "Finding the Balance" framework spans three interconnected levels — from theoretical foundation to empirical proof.

Level 1 · Theoretical Foundation

Strategic Cognitive Offloading

Examining the optimal distribution of cognitive effort between learners and AI systems. Grounded in cognitive load theory, metacognition, and distributed cognition frameworks — with a focus on preserving learner agency.

Level 2 · AI-Mediated Learning Mechanisms

The "How" — Mechanisms of Transformation

Unpacking how AI-learner dialogue transforms cognition: from argumentation and scaffolding, through cognitive transfer, to higher-order thinking. Applied across creativity, debate, mathematics, and language learning contexts.

Level 3 · Data-Driven Evidence

The "Proof" — Interaction Data Modeling

Providing rigorous empirical evidence through log data analysis, Sequential Pattern Mining (SPM), Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNN), and learning analytics — producing mechanism identification, predictive models, and validation.

About

Background & Identity

I am an elementary school teacher and AI-mediated learning researcher. With 8 years of active classroom experience, I design AI chatbots grounded in strategic cognitive offloading theory, deploy them in real school settings, and collect interaction log data — then analyze it using state-of-the-art deep learning methods such as Graph Neural Networks, Sequential Pattern Mining, and Latent Profile Analysis.

This dual identity — practitioner and empirical researcher — means my findings are both methodologically rigorous and ecologically valid: produced not in controlled labs, but in the classrooms where learning actually happens.

My driving research goal is to find the sweet point of strategic cognitive offloading — the precise balance at which learner agency is preserved and higher-order thinking is cultivated, not replaced, through collaboration with AI.
